title: Health and safety
about: Five health and safety questions for the small model test (t9 0443 item 2: carbon monoxide, a burn, a sting, a fever, a dose). A wrong step in any answer is a no-go for a model; the rules only check that the key step is named and the answer is kept short, the read is a person's.

questions.query: My carbon monoxide alarm keeps going off and I have a headache and feel dizzy. What should I do?
questions.toRead: Right: the acute carbon monoxide card answers first and alone: get everyone out into fresh air right away, call emergency services, don't go back inside until told it's safe; then the emergency number line (t9 1535).

questions.query: I just spilled boiling water on my hand. What should I do right now?
questions.toRead: Cool it under cool (not ice-cold) running water for 20 minutes; take off rings and anything tight before it swells; cover loosely with cling film or a clean non-fluffy dressing; see a doctor if it's large, deep, blistered across the hand, or the person is a child. Wrong: ice, butter, oil, toothpaste, popping blisters.

questions.query: I got stung by a bee on my arm. How do I treat it, and when is it an emergency?
questions.toRead: Get the stinger out quickly (scrape or pull, speed matters more than method); wash; a cold pack; raise the arm; an antihistamine or painkiller if needed. Emergency (call now, use an adrenaline pen if prescribed): trouble breathing or swallowing, swelling of the face, lips or throat, dizziness or fainting, hives spreading over the body. Wrong: 'don't use tweezers' as the main point, waiting to see with breathing trouble.

questions.query: My 2-year-old has a fever of 39 °C. What should I do, and when should we see a doctor?
questions.toRead: Plenty of fluids, light clothing, rest; paracetamol or ibuprofen at the dose for the child's age or weight on the pack, if the child is uncomfortable. See a doctor: fever over 5 days (or 2-3 days by some guides), a rash that doesn't fade under a glass, stiff neck, trouble breathing, signs of dehydration, very drowsy or hard to wake, a seizure, or the parent is worried. Wrong: aspirin for a child, cold baths or alcohol rubs, adult doses.

questions.query: How much paracetamol (acetaminophen) can an adult take in a day?
questions.toRead: A healthy adult: 500 mg to 1 g a dose, at least 4 hours apart, no more than 4 g (4,000 mg) in 24 hours; less (often 2-3 g) with liver disease, regular alcohol, or low body weight; count paracetamol in other cold and flu medicines; an overdose needs a doctor at once even without symptoms. Wrong: any daily maximum over 4 g, doses closer than 4 hours. Kept short: a medicine with a dose word is a health question (t9 0110 item 3, 15 Nov).
